name: inventory
description: Things the player carries, with rules the game chooses. There is no inventory built in: a game declares as many containers as it wants (backpack, hotbar, equipment, chest), makes as many slots as it wants in each, and decides what each slot accepts, how big a stack it holds and whether it is locked. Items go into slots by gathering them, or by a Hand that picks one up and puts it down. How it looks is up to ui grids and sprites.

components.name: Slot
components.description: One place in a container. container names an item of the game's "container" list and index is the slot's number in it, from 0; together they are the slot's address. accepts is the set of categories (the game's "category" list) the slot takes: an item is taken when it has one of them, and an empty set takes everything: a slot that only holds weapons accepts ["weapon"]. max_stack caps the stack the slot holds (0: no cap beyond the item's own). A locked slot neither receives nor gives. The slot's Position is where its item is shown.

components.name: Item
components.description: Something that can be carried. kind names an item of the game's "item_kind" list; categories is the set of categories it belongs to; quantity is the size of the stack and max_stack the most that one stack of this kind holds (1 for things that do not stack). While stored is false the item lies in the world and a Gatherer can pick it up; once stored it is in the slot at the address container and slot, and is shown there (as part of the interface, not of the world): its Position follows the slot's, its Sprite and its Text become screen ones, and a Text on the item shows the quantity (put {value} in the text) while stored and is invisible while the item lies in the world. Slot indexes of a container are 0, 1, 2... without gaps.

components.name: Gatherer
components.description: Picks up the items that lie within radius of its Position into the container: each goes onto a stack of the same kind that has room, else into the first empty slot that accepts it. An item no slot can take stays where it is.

components.name: Transfer
components.description: A request to move the item of one slot to another, possibly in another container. Spawn an entity with one; the next tick it is carried out and status becomes 1 (done) or 2 (refused: no item, a locked or unsuitable slot, a stack that is full, an item that does not fit back when swapping). Onto an empty slot the whole stack moves; onto the same kind the stacks merge as far as the room goes; onto another kind the two items swap places if both slots take the other's item. The request disappears a tick later.

components.name: Hand
components.description: The cursor of a player over one container: left, right, up and down (actions of the game) move it over the slots, columns slots to a row; select picks up the item under it, then puts it down on the next slot it is pressed on (the Transfer rules apply: it merges, swaps or is refused); cancel lets go. With use_pointer the pointer (the actions pointer_x and pointer_y, in pixels) moves it to the slot it is over, in slots slot_width by slot_height big, and click acts as select. An action left out is none: it does nothing. The Hand's own Position follows the slot under it (give it a Sprite as a frame) and its Sprite shows cell cursor_frame, or holding_frame while an item is held.

systems.name: hand
systems.description: Moves every Hand, and picks up or puts down the item under it.

systems.name: transfer
systems.description: Carries out the Transfer requests and removes the ones that were answered a tick ago.

systems.name: gather
systems.description: Puts the items near a Gatherer into its container.

systems.name: show
systems.description: Shows each stored item on its slot, as part of the interface, and each loose item in the world.
